title: MNAR-k-means: A k-means Clustering for Data Missing Not at Random with Magnitude-Decaying Probability
summary: The paper addresses k-means clustering for incomplete data under missing-not-at-random mechanisms, where k-POD-style mean imputation biases cluster centers. It proposes MNAR-k-means, which adds a penalty on imputed values at missing positions, interprets this as maximizing a magnitude-decaying missingness probability, and optimizes the loss by alternating updates with linear complexity. Experiments on synthetic and real data show lower CER and MSE than k-POD and several imputation baselines, with theoretical consistency results for the estimated centers.

match_target.why: The user hint points to Figure 2 (k=2, a=2, lambda*=0.1), but that panel is graphical and prints no exact CER value. Among numeric claims, C1 is the cheapest central comparison showing the paper's proposed-vs-k-POD improvement: Lymphoma n=62, proposed 0.029 vs k-POD 0.279.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: Table 3 reports SD 0.01 for the target C1 value, so the absolute band is 3 x 0.01 = 0.03.

requirements.stmt: Implement the unconstrained MNAR-k-means objective with binary memberships U and U1_k=1_n.
Use the expanded loss summing observed squared residuals plus lambda times squared center values at missing positions.
Update each membership by assigning the point to the center minimizing observed squared distances plus lambda times missing-feature center squares.
Update each center coordinate as observed assigned sum divided by observed assigned count plus lambda times missing assigned count.
Generate synthetic MNAR missingness with observed probability 1-exp(-lambda* x_ij^2), equivalently missing probability exp(-lambda* x_ij^2).
requirements.quote: Pr (xij is observed | x1, . . . , xn) = 1 −exp(−λ∗x2 ij)

requirements.stmt: Initialize centers by column-mean imputation followed by k-means++ on the imputed complete matrix.
requirements.quote: First, we impute missing values of X by corresponding columns’ means of observed values

requirements.stmt: Evaluate clustering with the pairwise Classification Error Rate definition.
Evaluate center estimation error by sum_l min_l' squared Euclidean distance between estimated and true centers.
requirements.quote: MSE( c M, M ∗∗) = Pk l=1 minl′=1,...,k ∥ˆμl −μ∗∗ l′ ∥2
